messages.subject: setarTest with external Threshold?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm new to the tsDyn package and hoping to better understand it's functionality.

I understand that if I specify a SETAR model with an external threshold variable, then I am actually specifying the standard TAR model. So when I specify;
     mod.setar <-setar(data, m=5, d=1, thDelay=1, thVar=data$x)
the model is actually a TAR model and not a SETAR model. Please correct me if I'm wrong, as I'm a newbie to this stuff.

So I guess I'm wondering why there is not an option to specify an external threshold variable in the setarTest? When performing a test of linearity against a threshold, Hansen showed that F-tests are not chi-squared distributed, thus the need for bootstrapping. Maybe I missed something in the Hansen paper. Did Hansen's result only apply to the endogenously determined threshold variables (i.e. only the lagged dep vars) ??

messages.subject: STAR problem, threshold variable out of range
messages.subject_clean: STAR problem, threshold variable out of range
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

It appears I'm having a problem with the STAR package. When fitting a STAR, I obtain an estimate for threshold value which is out of the range of my data. My threshold variable ranges from -1.064 to 0.7825, yet I am getting an estimate of -2.981096 for a threshold value. This must be an error right?

mod[["star"]] <- star(rin$lrd4, m=11, thDelay=2, thVar=rin$lrd6)

Testing for addition of regime 3.
  Estimating gradient matrix...
  Done. Computing the test statistic...
  Done. Regime 3 is needed (p-Value =  1.538072e-05 ).
Adding regime  3 .
Fixing good starting values for regime  3 ...
Reordering regimes...
Estimating parameters of regime 3 ...
Optimized values fixed for regime  3 : gamma =  3.622673 , th =  -2.981096
*** Convergence problem. Code:  10

However, the estimated threshold value is not possible given the threshold variable that I specified. As you can see in the summary statistics, the minimum value of my theshold variable is -1.064

summary(rin$lrd6)
      Min.    1st Qu.     Median       Mean    3rd Qu.       Max.
-1.0640000 -0.0262000 -0.0037360 -0.0004353  0.0214300  0.7825000

Are the problems coming from the Convergence Code 10??

messages.subject: modifying STAR and SETAR to include Exogenous variables
messages.subject_clean: modifying STAR and SETAR to include Exogenous variables
messages.body_plain:
Hi

I would like to modify the STAR and SETAR codes to allow for the inclusion of exogenous variables. I'm not well versed in R, but past posts imply this should be a straight forward task.

https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups#!searchin/tsdyn/exogenous/tsdyn/g4bvguZ_fTQ/Vd5NnH0mOAoJ

" you should seek to replace simply the xxL, xxH (line 85-86) and th by your own regressors. Adapting the code from there should require little changes, do not look at lines after 246, since these are specific to tsDyn. "

But then I find somewhat conflicting comments from another post which makes the task seem rather arduous.

https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups#!searchin/tsdyn/exogenous/tsdyn/ts-FZgL6D8E/g8V7RKAnYKEJ

"If you were to modify lstar() yourself, you should modify several lines, the most important being 85 and 86:
xxL <- cbind(const,xx[,1:mL])

then add your regressors. YOu will need probably to modify the code at several other places, to take into account the fact that you have more regressors, hence parameter naming might fail. You will in any case not be able to use the predict() since the predict use a loop starting from zero to re-create the series. This would require significant changes.

Good luck"

Has anybody had any luck with this? Matthieu are you still the keeper of tsDyn? Can anybody provide me with some guidance?

messages.subject: Re: [tsDyn] setarTest with external Threshold?
messages.body_plain:
Hi

Sorry for the late answer(s). You are right, by specifying thVar, this is using an external threshold variable. And yes, it would make sense to have the option in setarTest! This is however pretty straightwofrward: look for all instances of setar/selectSETAR in the code, and add the optional argument thVar. Let us know if you have some difficulties!

Best

Matthieu

messages.subject_clean: [tsDyn] STAR problem, threshold variable out of range
messages.body_plain:
Yes, this is indeed an error, as flagged by the convergence code 10!

star() uses function optim(), look on optim() page at what this code means, then use trace=TRUE, and try to specify the control=list() argument to get convergence!

Good luck!

Matthieu
